_methodology_note: Retrieval-quality benchmarking at the originally planned scope (14 hard queries x 3 users, matching run_benchmark.py's own hard-tier slice) hung indefinitely partway through in this sandboxed environment on repeated attempts, with zero CPU/network activity (not a correctness bug: a single run_query() call, and small batches of 5 queries x 1 user, both complete reliably every time -- this looks like resource accumulation across many sequential calls within one long-lived process, not a bug in the pipeline itself). Local backend's retrieval-quality number below is a reliably reproduced 5-query x 1-user sample. The cloud backend hit this project's well-documented free-tier Gemini rate-limit issue (see REPORT.md section 8.1) on the same reduced sample after 1 query completed; rather than keep fighting an infrastructure constraint, its retrieval-quality row below is the already-validated, larger (14 hard queries x 3 users = 42 runs) hard-tier result from eval/results/retrieval_quality_summary.json, generated earlier in this project with the cloud backend -- same eval set, same difficulty slice, larger and more robust sample, just not from this exact script. Not a strictly apples-to-apples n, but directionally sound and clearly labeled.
